issues.description: Constructor parameter order for class Lecture is inconsistent between the problem statement (UML/instructions) and the provided solution implementation. The problem statement / UML (problem_statement.md) requires the constructor parameters to follow the attribute order: (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) declares the constructor as: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents). This difference in parameter order can confuse students about the expected constructor signature and lead to incorrect instantiation or mismatches with instructional text/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter order consistent with the UML/instructions or update the UML/instructions to match the implementation. Preferred fix for clarity: change the solution constructor signature to: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) and update the assignments inside the constructor accordingly. Alternatively, if the implementation order is intentional, update the problem statement (lines showing constructor requirements and the UML) to reflect the implemented order and ensure any template stubs and tests use the same signature.
